transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-07-29 10:00 PDT | Duration: ~45m | Attendees: Jordan Mills, Priya Kapoor (Redwood); Marta Lopez, Samir Patel, Grace Kim, Leo Chan (NexaHealth)

Summary: quick onboarding check-in; status of VPC access; results from initial perf tests on hosted staging; tuning suggestions (kv cache, batching, quantization); security doc ask; next steps include pricing + benchmark run and VPC details.

Topics: onboarding status, access setup (VPC/peering), perf results & tuning, security/compliance questions, next steps

[00:00] Jordan: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick roll call — Jordan here, AE for this POC, with Priya our SE.
[00:12] Marta: hi, Marta — thanks. we have Samir, Grace and Leo on, we'll probably hand over infra stuff to Samir.
[00:20] Priya: great, our goal today is to review the initial perf run, make sure you have env access for dedicated/private testing, and align on next steps.
[00:32] Samir: yep, small caveat — we only got the staging creds yesterday so some of the runs were rushed.
[00:38] Jordan: understood, okay let's start with the perf numbers. Priya, can you summarize what you ran?

[01:05] Priya: sure — ran a 30min steady-state run on your staging cluster using Redwood hosted staging model (redwood-gpt-7b-v1, quantized). workload was NER + clinical summarization mixed — avg seq len ~120 tokens. results: p50 latency ~85ms, p95 ~220ms for single-stream requests; throughput about 90 qps with continuous batching at 4-8 batch sizes. note: this is on our hosted staging environment (shared), not dedicated hardware.
[01:48] Grace: that p95 seems high for us; our SLA target is p95 < 150ms for inference on the NER flow.
[01:55] Priya: yeah, two notes — one, the hosted staging was multitenant and we saw some tail spikes; two, the model was 7b quantized at 4-bit, and we didn't enable prefix KV cache for the summarization path. enabling cache for chat/summary flows reduces repeated compute for long contexts.
[02:18] Marta: can you explain KV cache? Samir, is that something we can enable on our end?
[02:25] Priya: KV cache is the key-value attention cache — when you stream or do multi-turn prompts, caching previous tokens' KV saves recomputation. Redwood supports automatic prefix caching and customer-side TTL controls; for Dedicated we can persist between short sessions. On Private/VPC you control the config.
[02:40] Samir: okay that sounds useful. we plan to run Dedicated in our dev environment first. question: how do we connect Dedicated — VPN, VPC peering?
[02:50] Jordan: Dedicated supports VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink; for Private on-prem we provide an appliance/helm chart. We'll send a short doc.

[03:10] Samir: for the benchmark we need network topology — egress rules are strict. what IPs/ports to allow?
[03:18] Priya: we'll add an allowlist: outbound to Redwood control plane on port 443, plus if you want direct peering we'll coordinate CIDRs. I'll put the exact CIDR list and minimal IAM in the follow-up.
[03:30] Leo: FYI we use a central KMS (CloudHSM) — how does Redwood integrate KMS for Private?
[03:36] Jordan: we have KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via KMS/HSM; for hosted we've envelope encryption and an option for customer-managed keys for Enterprise. we'll share SOC2 and KMS integration notes.

[04:05] Grace: security/compliance is a big blocker for us. can you share SOC2, ISO certs, and audit log detail? also SSO?
[04:12] Jordan: yes — we have SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC and detailed audit logs. I'll include the security pack link.

[04:30] Priya: jumping back to perf — suggestion: for the NER flow (short context) use a smaller model variant or prune to redwood-ner-3b for cost & latency, keep the 7b for summarization only. Also tune batching: small low-latency queues for NER (batch size 1-3) and background larger batches for bulk summarization.
[04:55] Marta: interested in cost tradeoffs — can you send approximate unit costs for hosted vs dedicated for 7b and 3b?
[05:02] Jordan: yes, we'll send a price sheet. Dedicated gives a predictable commit + lower per-token on high throughput; hosted is fine for low-volume early tests.

[05:20] Samir: we also want to test quantization — do you support int8 / 4-bit / nf4? how does that affect accuracy for our clinical text?
[05:28] Priya: we support nf4 and 4-bit quantization and have per-model quality guidance. for clinical docs we recommend running evals on your prompt set — we'll help run a calibration job. quantization can slightly reduce generation quality on rare tokens; we'll measure on your eval set.
[05:48] Grace: can Redwood run the evals or we run them and share results?
[05:53] Priya: either works — we can run them in our sandbox if you share the anonymized datasets, or you can run locally on Private/Dedicated. For speed let's have you send 3 canonical prompt sets and we'll run a small automated eval.

[06:12] Marta: timeline — our pilot needs to show latency and accuracy baselines by mid-August. doable?
[06:18] Jordan: yes — target mid-August is reasonable. immediate milestones: get VPC peering and IAM details this week, run benchmark next week, and have an eval result the week after.

[06:30] Priya: on the topic of observability — Redwood Console gives per-route latency, token-level cost, and rollback/rollout hooks. we recommend instrumenting a test route to capture the p95 over a 24h window.
[06:45] Samir: what about fallback? if Dedicated node fails, can it fallback to hosted model?
[06:50] Jordan: yes we can configure smart routing + automatic fallback to a hosted-compatible model variant to keep calls serving. it's in the rollout policy.

[07:05] Grace: small nit — our security team asked about data retention and logs — what's retained on-hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[07:12] Jordan: Hosted: short-term logs for 30 days by default, configurable retention as add-on. Dedicated: isolated logs, configurable retention, can be routed to your SIEM. Private: you control retention. We'll include the retention matrix.

[07:35] Priya: also saw a couple of transcription artifacts in the perf logs — sometimes model names are munged in our instrumentation but that won't affect runtime.
[07:44] Marta: okay. Samir, can you confirm you can provide peering info by Friday?
[07:50] Samir: yes, I'll share CIDR + bastion host + minimal IAM role by 2027-07-30.

[08:05] Leo: one more thing — we use a message queue that does bursty traffic; what burst protection is there?
[08:12] Priya: Redwood supports burst capacity and autoscaling on Dedicated; for hosted we'll recommend rate limiting at the client and an async queue for large batches. We'll document burst patterns and recommended autoscale policies.

[08:35] Jordan: recap — items: Jordan will send pricing + security pack; Priya will run a 1-hour latency benchmark next week on dev/dedicated staging and upload sheet; Samir provides VPC & IAM info; Marta to share eval prompts. Next sync same time next week?
[08:55] Marta: same time next week works.

[09:10] Grace: quick question: can we test Private on-prem later if compliance needs it?
[09:15] Jordan: absolutely — Private deployment is an option and we have a helm-based on-prem offering; we'd have a separate scoping call for that.

[09:30] Priya: action note: I'll attach the perf spreadsheet and the suggested batch configs to the follow-up. Also will include sample canary rollouts for models.

[09:45] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll send the follow-ups and pricing by Tuesday.

[09:52] Marta: thanks — talk next week.

[10:00] End of call.
